items.title: Martin Gore and Cliff Damavandi share ‘Cross Whisper’ remixes by ANNA and Vera Grace
items.summary: Martin Gore and Cliff Damavandi share two remixes of "Cross Whisper" by ANNA and Vera Grace, ahead of a 12" vinyl release on Mute on December 4, 2026.
items.fullText:
Depeche Mode founding member Martin Gore and artist and lyricist Cliff Damavandi have shared two remixes of their single “Cross Whisper”, released as MG x CD + JL = with vocals from Gore’s daughter, Johnnie Lee. Lisbon-based Brazilian artist ANNA and Dutch DJ and modular synthesist Vera Grace each contributed a remix, out now on Mute ahead of a 12″ vinyl pressing of the single on December 4, 2026.

ANNA, who has previously remixed Depeche Mode and Martin Gore, describes her remix as resonating with playful positivity: “This remix came together after I had just spent five days at Ozora Festival, dancing, connecting with people and getting so inspired by the music, powerful grooves and energy there. I came back really excited to get into the studio and create something on that psychedelic vibe. And then Martin’s stems arrived, fitting perfectly with what I had in mind. I made the remix so quickly and had so much fun doing it! I was dancing and jumping around the studio while creating it.” Vera Grace took the track in a different direction: “I enjoy a challenge, especially when it pushes me outside my comfort zone. This was definitely one of those moments. The vocals and the different elements in the original track gave me a lot of room to experiment and play around with different ideas. I built several distinct parts, eventually bringing them together into one piece: a section driven by chords, and another where atmospheric bleeps drift through the drums, taking me in a different direction from what I usually explore in my techno productions.”

The forthcoming 12″ vinyl adds remixes from techno artist, DJ and label head Regis, British hauntologist Pye Corner Audio (Martin Jenkins) and boothnavy alongside the ANNA and Vera Grace versions, spread across both sides with the original track. “Cross Whisper” opens with whispered voices that give way to Gore’s synths. The song grew out of a story Gore has told about birds appearing around the deaths of people and pets close to him. Damavandi wrote the lyrics after hearing Gore recount it. The pre-order for the vinyl is available via Mute.

About Martin Gore and Cliff Damavandi

Martin Gore is a songwriter, electronic composer and founding member of Depeche Mode, and has released solo and collaborative material on Mute alongside his work with the band. Cliff Damavandi is an artist and lyricist who wrote the words to “Cross Whisper” after Gore shared the story behind the song. The pair released ‘Cross Whisper’ as MG x CD + JL = on October 20, 2026, with vocals from Gore’s daughter Johnnie Lee. The ANNA and Vera Grace remixes, together with the additional versions arriving on the December 4 vinyl pressing, extend that single into a full remix project on Mute.

items.title: Corlyx release ‘Die Young’ feat. Mark Gemini Thwaite, open ‘The Crimson Tapes’ pre-order
items.summary: Corlyx release the single "Die Young" featuring Mark Gemini Thwaite via Out Of Line Music, and open pre-orders for the album "The Crimson Tapes."
items.fullText:
Death pop band Corlyx released the single “Die Young”, featuring guitarist Mark Gemini Thwaite (The Mission, Tricky, Peter Murphy), on November 12, 2026 via Out Of Line Music. The single’s release opens pre-orders for Corlyx’s new studio album, “The Crimson Tapes,” due March 19, 2027 on jewelcase CD.

“Die Young” pairs Corlyx’s post-punk atmosphere with Thwaite’s guitar work: flamenco-style acoustic guitars inspired by John McGeoch, layered with his electric touches. The lyrics speak for a generation running out of hope, set against a world that keeps falling apart. Thwaite joined the track at demo stage. “When Caitlin invited me to record some guitar ideas for ‘Die Young’ by Corlyx, in its demo stage, I was struck by the energy of the song and its post-punk atmosphere,” he recalls, “looking forward to hearing it on the dancefloor!” Singer Caitlin Stokes calls the collaboration a personal milestone: “I believe in magical moments, it was iconic enough to just have this collab happen with such a personal inspiration to me, MGT’s resume is insane, and what we made together was so cohesive and elevated. I am still pinching myself that this experience, this work of art we created together happened.”

“The Crimson Tapes” runs 13 tracks, soaked in post-punk, dream pop and alt-rock, with songs including “Sweeter Than Blood,” “More Anarchy,” “Palest Shade,” “Die Young” (feat. MGT), “Broke Girl,” “The Holy Vampire,” “Your Heart In The Serpent’s Mouth,” “Pussycat,” “Chains (Ode To Frankenstein’s Monster),” “Belial,” “Ride The Rocket,” “No Rights” and “Left In The Cold.” It follows Corlyx’s double album “Purple Pain” (2025) and arrives after the singles “The Holy Vampire,” “Your Heart In The Serpent’s Mouth” and “More Anarchy.”

About Corlyx

Corlyx are a “death pop” band originally from Los Angeles, now based between the UK and Turin, fronted by singer-songwriter Caitlin Stokes alongside guitarist and producer Brandon Ashley and bassist Davide Rocco, with drummer Flow Toulman now on board. The band’s third studio album, “Purple Pain,” a 19-track double album, was released via Out Of Line Music on February 14, 2025, and followed by the singles “The Holy Vampire” and “Your Heart In The Serpent’s Mouth”. Corlyx have toured Europe, the UK and the US with Blutengel, Twin Tribes, Double Echo and Unzucht, and have collaborated with Lord Of The Lost, Massive Ego and Ashbury Heights. With “Die Young” and “The Crimson Tapes,” Corlyx stay rooted in the underground while adding Mark Gemini Thwaite’s guitar work to the mix.

items.title: Instinct and Pain sign to Morella Records, ‘Mauvaises Pensées’ due in March
items.summary: Sardinian gothic rock trio Instinct and Pain sign to Morella Records; album "Mauvaises Pensées" arrives March 5, 2027, with a single on December 4.
items.fullText:
Gothic rock and darkwave trio Instinct and Pain have signed to Morella Records, the label announced on November 12, 2026. The Sardinian band’s new ten-song album, “Mauvaises Pensées,” will be released on Bandcamp and major streaming platforms on March 5, 2027. The first single and its music video, “The Death of Love,” arrive on December 4, 2026, followed by a second single in January 2027 and a third in February.

“Mauvaises Pensées” takes its title from a collection of thoughts by the French poet and writer Paul Valéry, whose ideas inspired most of the record’s songs. Its sound moves from punk to alternative metal to folk, with goth running through as the common thread. The album was recorded at Tore Cabiddu Studio and mixed and mastered at Cut Fire Mix Studio. Family members of the band guest on the title track, playing keyboards, violin and clarinet.

“Instinct and Pain is a three-year-old band that sounds like they’ve been together for decades. The music is riveting, pure gothic post-punk, the vocals are brilliant and the musicianship is top notch. I’m honored to call Instinct and Pain a Morella family member,” said Blake Carpenter, founder of Morella Records. “We would like people to hear our voice, what we feel through music, and the passion and commitment we put into making these songs,” said Alessandro Manca of Instinct and Pain.

Reviewers have previously described the band’s take on goth rock as one “that never lapses into plagiarism or, worse, affected penmanship,” according to Ver Sacrum, while Hardsounds called them “one to keep an eye on” and Mick Mercer described them as “vibrant Sardinian goth.” Instinct and Pain’s music is available on Bandcamp and Spotify.

About Instinct and Pain

Instinct and Pain are a gothic rock and darkwave trio from Ghilarza, in central Sardinia, Italy, formed in 2023 by Alessandro Manca (vocals, guitar), Luca Porcu (bass) and Nicola Loi (drums). The band builds its songs on dark atmosphere and melancholic melody, with post-punk bones and a debt to the darker side of the 1980s underground, citing Bauhaus, Joy Division, The Cure, Death In June, Christian Death and The Mission among its reference points. Instinct and Pain released their debut album, “All Is Gone,” independently in September 2024, and followed it with a cover of Pink Floyd’s “Lucifer Sam” in January 2026. Morella Records, an independent label for gothic rock, post-punk, deathrock and darkwave founded by Blake Carpenter, is now the band’s home for “Mauvaises Pensées,” their second album and first release for the label.

items.title: The Halo Trees release ‘Until I Disappear’ ahead of ‘Downfalls’ album
items.summary: The Halo Trees release the single "Until I Disappear" via Cop International, ahead of the album "Downfalls," due in February 2027.
items.fullText:
Berlin-based post-punk and indie rock band The Halo Trees released the single “Until I Disappear” on 6 November 2026 via Cop International. The track is the first preview of the band’s new album, “Downfalls,” set for release in February 2027 on the same label.

“Until I Disappear” moves between dark indie rock, post-punk and atmospheric textures. Lyrically, the song deals with alienation and identity, following a protagonist who finds parts of their own identity missing. Singer and guitarist Sascha Blach explains the premise: “The experience of being trapped in a world that feels unfamiliar, cut off from one’s true origin. Alienation – from the world, from other people and ultimately from oneself.” The song leaves open whether that protagonist left something behind “on the other side,” and as on the rest of “Downfalls,” the question goes unanswered, pointing instead toward a broader search for truth and meaning that runs through the album.

“Until I Disappear” is available as a download on Bandcamp and across major streaming platforms, including a Dolby Atmos mix. Sascha Blach wrote, recorded, mixed and mastered the track at Winter Solitude Studio in Berlin between 2024 and 2026, and also created the single’s artwork. The Halo Trees’ current lineup is Sascha Blach on vocals, guitar and synths, Stefan Helwig on drums, Gabriel Wohlfahrt on bass and Georges-Emmanuel Schneider on violin. The song is published by 777songs/Schubert Music Publishing GmbH.

About The Halo Trees

The Halo Trees are a post-punk and indie rock band from Berlin, led by singer, guitarist and producer Sascha Blach. The band’s sound sits between The National, Nick Cave and Editors, pairing dark indie rock with post-punk structure and atmospheric production. The Halo Trees returned with the album ‘Where The Deep Ends’ in 2024, and later that year launched the remix album ‘Electric Mirror’ ahead of a European tour with Frontline Assembly. “Until I Disappear” is the band’s first new material since that remix record, and the opening statement for “Downfalls,” their next full-length for Cop International.

items.title: Sebastian Komor interview: on Icon of Coil, SRK Group and fatherhood
items.summary: Sebastian Komor discusses Icon of Coil's new album, SRK Group, working with Alphaville, fatherhood and film scoring in this Side-Line interview.
items.fullText:
Sebastian Komor has worked across the electronic and industrial music scene for decades, through Icon of Coil alongside Andy LaPlegua and Christian Lund, Komor Kommando, SRK Group, and production and remix work for artists including Alphaville, KMFDM and Ayria. With new SRK Group material, an Icon of Coil album in progress and a live Icon of Coil appearance booked for Dark Force Fest in 2027, Side-Line spoke with Komor about that work, his years in Poland, Norway and Canada, fatherhood, film scoring, and his view of how the industrial scene has changed since the late 1990s.

Sebastian Komor interview

Sebastian, you’ve been involved in so many projects over the years that I sometimes wonder whether even you can keep track of them all. Icon of Coil, Komor Kommando, SRK Group, countless productions and remixes… After all these years, what still makes you sit down and think, “I need to make some noise”? And is there anything you’ve reached the point of never wanting to do again?

Komor: It is who I am. It is in my blood. Despite the moments when I sit in the studio thinking, “I can’t do this anymore!”, I have, at this stage in life, concluded that my path in life is music and sound, in whatever capacity that may exist moving forward. It’s that fire within. The flame that never dies.

There’s a certain Komor sound that’s pretty hard to miss, even when you’re working with somebody else. You’ve worked with artists ranging from Alphaville to KMFDM, and more recently produced Ayria’s “13 Stitches.” When does helping an artist find their sound turn into putting too much of yourself into it? And which collaboration has pushed you furthest outside your comfort zone?

Komor: I would say working with Alphaville was the one that pushed me the most. I think the pressure I felt had something to do with it. Sitting next to the man who sang “Forever Young” and “Big in Japan,” holding the original tapes of those songs in my hands, was one of the greatest experiences of my career. Once you connect with the people behind the music and learn who they are, what excites them, what inspires them, that’s when magic happens.

I keep hearing that I have a sound. Still, to this day, I am not sure what that is, but it’s a good thing. Authenticity and personality are key, even more so in the days of AI. When I am in the producer’s chair, for me it’s a balance between doing what I am asked to, circling back to that certain sound, and listening to what the song itself says, all while having dialogues with the artist. Sometimes I get raw, minimal demos. In those cases, the vocals and the overall feel dictate what seems right, while I stay open to radically different ideas and sounds than one would “usually” use.

SRK Group has been making some noise with “Spitfire” and “Bleeding Heartsicle.” What’s happening in that head of yours at the moment? Is there a bigger plan behind these releases, or do you prefer the freedom of doing whatever you fancy? And should we assume Komor Kommando and your other projects are quietly plotting something in the background?

Komor: At the moment, my head is filled with ideas, negotiations and recalibrations. Musically and personally, I’ve always been more of an observer, that guy sitting in the corner, watching, listening, picking up on body language and patterns, making notes. When it comes to SRK Group, there is a goal we’re building towards, with the current focus on releasing one single a month. Komor Kommando is absolutely overdue for a new EP; plenty of tracks are in a demo stage. Then there is what is now official and public: a new Icon of Coil album in the making.

Born in Poland, raised in Norway, and eventually making Canada your home. That’s quite a few different worlds to grow up and live in. When someone asks where you’re from, is there even a simple answer anymore? And how much have those different cultures influenced not just your music, but your values, your worldview and the way you deal with people?

Komor: All vastly different countries and cultures indeed. Music is the bridge between them all. No matter where in the world you are, music finds a way to connect and unite people. The one thing about having lived in three different countries is that sense of never finding “home,” or a sense of where home is. Once I became a father, I found it. My son is the key, the light. In the last year or so, I have discovered that home is not external. Home is within. I am grateful for the path of Poland, Norway and Canada, and for the travelling that came with music: seeing the best and worst in people, experiencing the various cultures, speaking with people from all walks of life.

Icon of Coil still means an awful lot to people, even after more than twenty years. But here’s something I’ve been wondering: do you ever feel that some fans are still attached to the Sebastian they knew back then, while the actual Sebastian has moved on? And is there anything about those days you genuinely miss, or are you quite happy to leave certain things in the past?

Komor: People tend to lock onto fragments of time, or imply that the person on stage and in the music is my entire self. It’s the nature of things, I guess, when people know you for what you do, not you as a person. Icon of Coil was and will always be a big part of my career and history, a history I am proud of, considering all the sacrifices over the years it took to get there. That being said, becoming a father was a pivotal point in my life; the benefits of working from home made it possible. My son even helped with promo photos for Komor Kommando. Introducing him to music is magical; he loves Kraftwerk and Deadmau5. Icon of Coil, the complete live band, will be performing live at Dark Force Fest in 2027, the first time in about fifteen years.

You recently remixed “We Bring the Beat” for Aesthetic Perfection. Daniel Graves isn’t exactly famous for playing by the rules of any particular genre, and neither are you. How did you two end up working together, and what happens when two people who don’t particularly care about musical boundaries cross paths?

Komor: The first time we met must have been back in 2001. I heard “We Bring the Beat” on YouTube and immediately thought it was a killer song, so I asked if he would be down with me doing a remix of it for the hell of it. I appreciate his no-holds-barred approach to his sound and style. He found his thing, and it’s working. We also end up nerding out about music, music tools and tricks of the trade.

You’ve remixed everyone from Front Line Assembly and Nitzer Ebb to Apoptygma Berzerk and VNV Nation. Which remix are you personally most proud of, regardless of whether anyone else agrees? And who’s still on your dream collaboration list, living or dead?

Komor: The best I can do is a top three, in random order, from the perspective of the remixes I am happiest with sonically, and what they meant for me personally and career-wise: Celldweller – “Into the Void”; Rammstein – “Sonne”; Front Line Assembly – “Unleashed”, since FLA was a massive inspiration and this was closing a circle. Honourable mentions go to Apoptygma Berzerk‘s “Suffer in Silence” and Alphaville’s “To Germany with Love.” Dream collaborations: Hans Zimmer, Joel Zimmerman, Trent Reznor, Björk and Tool. Working on an alternative electro album with David Bowie or Kurt Cobain would also be amazing.

Your work has also taken you into sound design, film scoring and music for television. Quite a different playground from making people sweat on a dancefloor. Was there ever a project that made you think, “How the hell did I end up doing this?” And is there some completely different creative territory you’d still love to explore?

Komor: I’ve always been fascinated by film scoring. Maybe that is also part of how I ended up in the world of industrial, EBM and techno music, through sound design, the art of sampling, using any source as an instrument to convey an emotion or scenario. What I love most about music for film and TV is how non-formulaic and free from a grid it is, with tempo changes and an ebb and flow that work to evoke emotion. I have had the pleasure of working on some AAA Hollywood movies, helping out with some scenes, bending time and space, working off timecode rather than a set BPM.

You’ve watched the electronic and industrial scene change over several decades. Some things have moved forward, others seem permanently stuck somewhere around 1998. What do you think the scene seriously needs to get over? And what’s something from those earlier days that you wish we hadn’t lost along the way?

Komor: I think politics have corrupted the scene, ripping apart what used to be united. Being someone who cut my teeth with no manual to go by, one thing I cherish is belonging to something understood by people all over the world. We were there for the music, the friendships, the appreciation for the art and culture, the excitement. As much as I appreciate technological advancements, spending so much time on phones and devices, being fed news around the clock and arguing with strangers, is not healthy for society. Lastly, you are not an artist if you rely on AI to write the music for you; you are denying yourself the joy of learning the craft.

When music is both your passion and your job, I imagine there must be days when you don’t want to hear another bloody beat. So what happens when Sebastian Komor closes the studio door? And what’s something about your everyday life that would completely destroy your industrial credibility if people found out?

Komor: Music is on my mind at all times, whether I want it to be or not. As my studio has been at home for over twenty years, it’s never really closed, which is a benefit and a curse, but great for quickly getting an idea down or jumping on projects at short notice. Regarding my industrial credibility: I rarely listen to industrial music anymore. Bands I listen to these days are Kraftwerk, Queens of the Stone Age, Rezz, Automatic, Gojira, BodyImage, Crowbar, and a Vancouver band called The Organist Collective.

Open mic: anything you’d like to get off your chest, clear up or talk about that hasn’t come up?

Komor: I do not care where you are from, what colour skin you have, what language you speak, what your gender is. None of that matters. What matters is how you treat others, and who you are as a human being. I wish everyone the best, and I hope that whatever is at the root of the hate in their hearts gets resolved. Life is precious. Be grateful for having one.

About Sebastian Komor

Sebastian Komor is an electronic and industrial music producer, born in Poland, raised in Norway and now based in Canada. He is best known as one half of Icon of Coil, the Norwegian electro-industrial act he formed with Andy LaPlegua and Christian Lund; the band’s 2025 reissue of “Serenity is the Devil” marked its 25th anniversary, and a new Icon of Coil album is now in the making, ahead of a live performance booked for Dark Force Fest in 2027, the band’s first live show in around fifteen years.

Komor also records as Komor Kommando and, more recently, as SRK Group, which has released the singles “Spitfire” and “Bleeding Heartsicle.” Beyond his own projects, he has produced and remixed artists across the industrial and synthpop spectrum, including Ayria’s “13 Stitches,” Aesthetic Perfection’s “We Bring the Beat,” Alphaville’s “To Germany with Love,” and tracks by Front Line Assembly, Nitzer Ebb, Apoptygma Berzerk, VNV Nation, Rammstein and Celldweller. He has also contributed production work to acts including Noctortoise and KMFDM, and has worked in sound design and scoring for film and television.

items.title: Nova Atarashi announce ‘Venus Dub’ album for Glass Modern Records
items.summary: Nova Atarashi, the trio of David J, Alex Novak and Tim Newman, release the album "Venus Dub" on CD and download via Glass Modern Records on 27 November 2026.
items.fullText:
Nova Atarashi release the album “Venus Dub” on CD and download via Glass Modern Records on 27 November 2026. The trio pairs Venus Fly Trap vocalist Alex Novak with bassist David J and musician/producer Tim Newman, and builds the record around On-U Sound-style dub production layered under post-punk songwriting.

David J plays bass; Novak sings; Newman handles the music. David J is the bass player of Bauhaus, Love and Rockets and The Jazz Butcher, and has led a solo career since the 1980s alongside collaborations with writer Alan Moore. Novak fronts Venus Fly Trap and has previously sung in Religious Overdose, Tempest, Attrition and Nova State Conspiracy. Newman is a longtime David J collaborator and has produced multiple Glass Modern releases, including “Love Is a Ghost.”

The band’s own reference points are African Head Charge, Mark Stewart and the Maffia, and the On-U Sound catalogue of dub-inflected post-punk.

Novak and David J have worked together before: Glass Modern released the Venus Fly Trap/Alex Novak retrospective “Mercurial 1978-2018,” and David J and Newman have also released the two-volume “Analogue Excavations and Dream Interpretations” series together on the same label. “Venus Dub” is Nova Atarashi’s first announced release as a trio.

About Nova Atarashi

Nova Atarashi brings together three musicians with overlapping histories on the UK post-punk and gothic rock scenes. David J co-founded Bauhaus in Northampton in 1978 and went on to form Love and Rockets with fellow Bauhaus members Daniel Ash and Kevin Haskins; he has also played with The Jazz Butcher and released solo material since the 1980s, including collaborations with the writer Alan Moore. Alex Novak fronts Venus Fly Trap, a UK act with roots reaching back to the 1980s, and has previously sung with Religious Overdose, Tempest, Attrition and Nova State Conspiracy; a Venus Fly Trap/Alex Novak retrospective, “Mercurial 1978-2018,” was released on Glass Modern Records. Tim Newman is a musician and producer who has worked repeatedly with David J on Glass Modern releases, including the two-volume “Analogue Excavations and Dream Interpretations” series.

As Nova Atarashi, the three musicians draw on dub production associated with On-U Sound, African Head Charge and Mark Stewart and the Maffia, applied to post-punk songwriting. “Venus Dub” is released on CD and download via Glass Modern Records on 27 November 2026.

items.title: Jo Montgomerie announces ‘Made To Appear’ album on Nite Hive
items.summary: Jo Montgomerie releases her piano-led album "Made To Appear" via Nite Hive on 13 November, with digital mastering by Agnes Haus and a cassette edition.
items.fullText:
Manchester-based composer Jo Montgomerie releases her new album “Made To Appear” through the Brighton label Nite Hive on 13 November 2026. The record is built around piano, electronics and field recordings, and arrives as a digital album and a limited cassette edition.

Montgomerie composed and recorded all of the material in Manchester, UK. Agnes Haus, another Nite Hive artist, mastered the digital version. Nite Hive founder Penelope Trappes described the album as “a beautiful collision of score work, laced with darkness,” and called it a record that “demonstrates her undeniably brilliant relationship with the piano.”

The tracklist for “Made To Appear” runs:

  1. Mourning Fog
  2. Processes Of Motion [Interlude]
  3. Dust & Sunlight
  4. The Point Of Contact Between Opposing Forces
  5. Falling Together
  6. Autorotation
  7. A Surprise Encounter [Interlude]
  8. Through Dreamlike States
  9. In Anticipation Of (R)Evolution
  10. Still Not Sleeping [Final Interlude]
  11. Wireless
  12. Late Night Lights
  13. Cold-Traps On Airless Bodies
  14. Closing Credits

The cassette edition adds two further bonus tracks exclusive to that format.

Nite Hive is an experimental cassette imprint run by and for women and gender-expansive artists, based in Brighton, UK, and founded by Penelope Trappes. Its roster also includes Patricia Wolf, Karen Vogt, Pefkin and Agnes Haus, who mastered Montgomerie’s digital release.

About Jo Montgomerie

Jo Montgomerie is a producer, sound engineer and music teacher based in Manchester, originally from South West Scotland. Her work uses repetition, drones and manipulation, built from piano, electronics and field recordings, and explores themes of feeling and connection through space and time.

Her Bandcamp catalogue includes the albums “Ephemeral Rituals,” “From Industry Home,” “Are You Supposed To Be In The Wild?” and “Early Works Pt. II,” alongside “Those Things Beyond & Within,” released via Brachliegen Tapes in 2022. “Made To Appear” moves away from the denser, noisier style of her recent work toward a clearer, more deliberate sound built around the piano as the lead instrument, and is her first release for Nite Hive.

items.title: Rodrigo dl Moral releases remastered ‘Déjate Llevar’, plans four-song EP
items.summary: Mexican synthpop artist Rodrigo dl Moral has issued a remastered "Déjate Llevar" on Spotify, billed as the lead single of a planned four-song EP.
items.fullText:
Rodrigo dl Moral, a synthpop, darkwave and electro-pop artist from Mexico, has released a remastered version of “Déjate Llevar” on Spotify. The platform lists the track’s release date as September 25, 2026, and its title as “Déjate Llevar – 2026 Remastered Version.” The artist describes it as the lead single of an upcoming four-song EP. No EP title or release date has been confirmed.

A remaster, not a new song

“Déjate Llevar” is not a newly written track. In the description accompanying the visualizer on his YouTube channel, Rodrigo dl Moral states that he wrote the song some time ago and returned to it in 2026 for a new mix. Translated from the original Spanish, the description reads in part: “I made this song a while back and today I wanted to return to it. [‘Déjate Llevar’] has always had something special for me, so I decided to give it a new turn and put out this remastered version. It doesn’t change the song’s essence. I just wanted to hear it with a cleaner, deeper sound, the way I imagined it from the start.”

This differs from the artist’s submission to Side-Line, which described the song only as the lead single of an upcoming EP, with “nostalgic synths, emotional vocals, club energy,” and did not mention that it is a remaster of an earlier recording. A confirmed date for the original, non-remastered version of “Déjate Llevar” has not surfaced.

The YouTube visualizer was uploaded on September 25, 2026, the same date Spotify lists for the remastered single. Both the video and the artist’s own tags mark the track as synthpop and dance-pop.

Format and availability

“Déjate Llevar” is confirmed available as a digital single on Spotify. No Bandcamp release exists for the track. The YouTube upload is a visualizer. It is the release’s official visual accompaniment. No separate music video has been confirmed.

A full tracklist and formal title for the planned four-song EP have not been confirmed. Rodrigo dl Moral’s submission to Side-Line states only that “Déjate Llevar” is its lead single.

About Rodrigo dl Moral

Rodrigo dl Moral is a synthpop, darkwave and electro-pop artist based in Mexico. Verifiable background on the artist is limited. No Discogs or Wikipedia entry exists for him, and Side-Line’s archive holds no prior coverage under either “Rodrigo dl Moral” or “Rodrigo Moral.”

The artist runs a YouTube channel under the handle @RodrigodlMoral and a Beacons.ai link page that directs to his Instagram, YouTube and TikTok profiles. According to the description he posted with the “Déjate Llevar” visualizer, the song was written before 2026 and set aside until this year, when he remastered it for a cleaner, more direct sound without altering its composition.

The remastered “Déjate Llevar,” released September 25, 2026, is the first release from Rodrigo dl Moral covered by Side-Line. The artist has said it will lead a four-song EP.

items.title: Suffer Well releases new single ‘Came Around’
items.summary: Los Angeles post-punk project Suffer Well releases the single "Came Around" through God Complex, streaming now on Spotify.
items.fullText:
Los Angeles musician and filmmaker Alex Delgado released “Came Around” under the name Suffer Well, through God Complex. The single is streaming now on Spotify.

A post-punk song about betrayal

“Came Around” follows the interval between believing life has settled into place and realizing someone has been quietly undermining it. Delgado has cited Joy Division, New Order and Interpol as influences on Suffer Well’s sound, which pairs rhythmic discipline with an unsettled, anxious vocal. “The song starts with finally feeling like your life is coming together, then someone comes along and upends it,” Delgado said of the track, which is set at the moment its narrator spots the person responsible for his unravelling life standing in a crowd.

Delgado both performs and directs under the Suffer Well name, overseeing the project’s music and visual identity himself. “Came Around” is available to stream on Spotify.

About Suffer Well

Suffer Well is the solo project of Los Angeles-based singer, bassist and filmmaker Alex Delgado, who also directs and designs productions. “Came Around,” released through God Complex, draws on the post-punk lineage of Joy Division, New Order and Interpol, carrying their interest in giving private anxiety a physical, rhythmic presence into Delgado’s own songwriting.

items.title: Barcelona duo Villanelle release video for debut single ‘Infrarosso’
items.summary: Barcelona dark synth duo Villanelle release the video for debut single "Infrarosso", via Carmilla Sioux's label From Hell To Disco.
items.fullText:
Barcelona dark synth duo Villanelle released the official video for debut single “Infrarosso” on 24 September 2026. The track came out digitally on 10 September through From Hell To Disco, the Barcelona label and event platform run by the duo’s Carmilla Sioux. Villanelle pairs Sioux, a bassist turned electronic producer, with vocalist and lyricist Jessica Bellomo.

“Infrarosso” is Villanelle’s debut release. Bellomo, an Italo-Argentine interdisciplinary artist who works across dark disco, electro, breakbeat, EBM, techno and trance, wrote the Italian-language lyrics and layered the synthesizers. Sioux, who moved from playing bass in the post-punk scene into DJing and production, built the track from its bassline outward. The song blends EBM and electro rhythms with melody-driven songwriting that draws on 1980s Italo disco, in a sound comparable to Pet Shop Boys, Ladytron and Boy Harsher.

Villanelle’s video for ‘Infrarosso’

The video for “Infrarosso” is directed by Nicole Krämer and arrived two weeks after the single’s digital release.

“Infrarosso” is also available to stream on Spotify.

About Villanelle

Villanelle formed in Barcelona after Bellomo relocated from Argentina and met Sioux. Sioux founded From Hell To Disco in 2024 as a label and event platform for underground electronic music, releasing records, podcasts and curated club nights; its first vinyl release was the various-artists compilation “Inferno Vol. 1.” She has performed at Urban Spree in Berlin, Radion in Amsterdam, Gare in Porto, Karmen Camina in Strasbourg and Moog in Barcelona, and has appeared at the Grauzone festival. “Infrarosso” is Villanelle’s first release as a duo, with a debut album planned for spring 2027.

items.title: Charm School reunites with Matia Simovich for new single ‘Desolation’
items.summary: Louisville post-punk band Charm School releases "Desolation," featuring INHALT's Matia Simovich, out 25 September 2026 on Bandcamp.
items.fullText:
Matia Simovich, the Los Angeles producer behind INHALT, wrote the music for “Desolation“, the new Charm School single released 25 September 2026 on Bandcamp. Andrew Sellers, the Louisville post-punk band’s frontman, supplies vocals and lyrics. Simovich previously handled drum programming on Charm School’s 2023 track “Simulacra”; “Desolation” is their first full writing collaboration.

The track pairs a steady EBM bassline with Italo-disco melodic phrasing, set under a compressed, metallic vocal treatment from Sellers. No label is named for the single; it is self-released through the band’s Bandcamp page.

‘Desolation’ leads toward a new Charm School EP

“Desolation” is the lead single from an EP that has not yet been named or given a release date. The EP will include Steve Albini’s alternate mix of “Simulacra,” recorded in 2023, before Albini’s death in May 2024. Simovich made his own alternate mix of “Simulacra” that year as well.

Charm School live dates in October

Charm School plays three shows in support of “Desolation”:

  • 1 October 2026 – Camp Spaceman, Louisville, KY
  • 2 October 2026 – Pilot Light, Knoxville, TN
  • 18 October 2026 – Oblivion, Los Angeles, CA

About Charm School

Charm School formed in Louisville, Kentucky, around Andrew Sellers, with Matt Filip, Drew English and Brian Vega. Sellers built the band’s sound out of Louisville’s punk and hardcore lineage – Slint, Will Oldham, Sunspring, Crain, Guilt and Rodan – combined with Chicago post-hardcore acts The Jesus Lizard and Shellac, and older post-punk groups PiL, The Fall and Fugazi.

The band released the single “Simulacra” in June 2023, followed by its debut EP, “Finite Jest,” that July. Steve Albini and Matia Simovich each recorded alternate mixes of “Simulacra” around the same time. Charm School’s debut LP, “Debt Forever,” followed on Surprise Mind on 24 January 2025, and the “Schadenfreude Ploy” EP arrived in early 2026. The band now describes itself as “LA via Louisville.”

“Desolation,” released 25 September 2026, reunites Sellers with Simovich and points toward a new EP that will finally give Albini’s shelved “Simulacra” mix a release.

items.title: Bitumen sets third album ‘Reality Red’ for 6 November, shares ‘Perffect Dress’ video
items.summary: Melbourne post-punk band Bitumen announces third album "Reality Red," out 6 November 2026 on It Records, and shares the video for "Perffect Dress."
items.fullText:
Five years after the industrial post-punk turn of “Cleareye Shining,” Melbourne band Bitumen announces its third album, “Reality Red,” due 6 November 2026 on It Records in digital and limited-edition transparent red vinyl. The album’s first single is “Perffect Dress,” out now with an official video.

“Reality Red” runs 8 tracks: “Scent of Angels,” “Minutes of Pure Joy,” “Perffect Dress,” “Silversound,” “Rites Private,” “Architect of the Overflow,” “Casino Black” and “Racing Leather.” The band is Kate Binning (vocals), Sam Varney, Bryce Maher (bouzouki) and Simon Maisch (backing vocals, recording and production).

Bitumen’s video for ‘Perffect Dress’

“Perffect Dress” was recorded by Maisch at Lily Street Studios in Coburg North, with Andy Huhtanen McEwan of Tongue Dissolver playing drums as a guest. It is the first Bitumen recording to use live drums alongside the band’s usual instrumentation, including Maher’s bouzouki. The video shows the band gathered around an open fire against corrugated metal, with overlapping close-ups of instruments and Binning’s performance. Band photography is credited to Emily Herbert.

About Bitumen

It Records has released all three Bitumen albums to date. The Melbourne band’s self-titled debut came out on 26 July 2016, recorded and mixed by Maisch, Binning, Maher and Varney at Magnet studio in Preston and Coburg; its 10 tracks included a cover of Public Image Ltd’s “Religion.” The 2021 follow-up, “Cleareye Shining,” moved the band further into industrial post-punk territory.

“Reality Red,” due 6 November 2026, is Bitumen’s third album and its first to feature a guest drummer. Binning’s lyrics on the record draw on both invented and real-life characters. “Perffect Dress,” the lead single, is out now with its official video.

items.title: Kind Kid releases dark synthpop single ‘Bleed’
items.summary: Kind Kid, the Brooklyn project of Julien Martinez, has released the dark synthpop single "Bleed," the last single before his album out October 9.
items.fullText:
Kind Kid, the Brooklyn, New York project of Julien Martinez, has released “Bleed”, a dark synthpop single available now through Bandcamp. “Bleed” is Martinez’s final single before his debut album, due October 9, 2026.

The track was recorded at Golden Dice Studios in Brooklyn, produced by Dutchrevz and Martinez, and mixed and mastered by Michele Ricci. Eighties synthpop structures carry a darker undertow, with eerie synth flourishes and cold, dissonant tones set against a steady dance beat, pulling toward the gothic electronics of Clan of Xymox and the modern darkwave of Boy Harsher.

“Bleed” is written from the position of someone left to process an argument after the other party has already walked away. “I thought of it as some metaphorical situation where someone’s been left behind after some sort of attack, left to ‘bleed,’” Martinez said. “Sometimes a situation can feel so much different to one person than the other.” The lyrics repeat images and phrases across the song, a structure that mirrors replaying an unresolved conflict rather than moving past it.

About Kind Kid

Kind Kid is the solo project of Julien Martinez, previously based in Texas and now working out of Brooklyn, New York. “Bleed” follows a series of singles released under the Kind Kid name and precedes Martinez’s debut album, scheduled for October 9, 2026. The project’s sound draws on eighties synthpop songwriting filtered through the darker textures of gothic and darkwave electronics.

items.title: Anton and Tout Debord share video for ‘Répression’
items.summary: Paris coldwave project Anton, led by Anton Steinbock, has released the single "Répression" with a video made with artist Tout Debord, out now on Bandcamp.
items.fullText:
Anton, the Paris-based coldwave project led by Anton Steinbock, has released “Répression”, a single out now on Bandcamp, together with an official video made with fellow coldwave artist Tout Debord. The track was produced by Leonid Diaghilev.

Ringing guitars and a firm, deliberate bassline anchor the song, with synths that lean toward the French coldwave lineage of Asylum Party and Little Nemo and a melancholic tone comparable to the Scottish band Lowlife. Steinbock delivers the vocal in a low, echoing register, moving between French and English across the track. The lyrics turn on despair, fixation and religious imagery, casting love as a transaction involving devotion, punishment and sacrifice: “Pray for me tonight / Blinded by your light / Stigmatize my mind / Your lost paradise.”

The video, directed by Tout Debord (Leonid Diaghilev) with additional cinematography by Sylvester Engbrox, layers performance footage over religious imagery, cemeteries and stone monuments. “Répression” follows the earlier single “Never Freed Myself” and continues the post-punk direction of Anton’s prior releases.

About Anton

Anton is the coldwave project of Anton Steinbock, based in Paris and active since 2024. The project’s debut release, the “Volcan” EP, came out on Detriti Records, followed by the “Glacier” EP on Icy Cold Records. Side-Line covered the combined edition, “Glacier / Volcan,” released in April 2025. Steinbock has since expanded Anton into a live configuration with Gabriela Guyez, performing material that ranges from harder post-punk to synth-driven darkwave. “Répression,” released in September 2026 in collaboration with Tout Debord, follows the single “Never Freed Myself” and is the project’s latest release.

items.title: Faded Pulse releases ethereal goth album ‘Elysia’
items.summary: Faded Pulse, the Washington, D.C. project of Faeryn Johnson, has released "Elysia," a second album mixing ethereal wave, goth, folk and dream pop.
items.fullText:
Faded Pulse, the Washington, D.C. project of Faeryn Johnson, has released “Elysia”, a second full-length that combines ethereal wave, goth, folk and dream pop. The album is out now through Bandcamp as a digital release.

Acoustic guitar, hammered dulcimer, electric bass and ambient synthesizer carry a set of songs built around water spirits, waiting maidens and woodland gatherings drawn from medieval poetry and Victorian painting. Johnson has a background in art history, and cites the Pre-Raphaelites, the Arts and Crafts movement and Art Nouveau as touchstones alongside the writing of Alfred Lord Tennyson, Samuel Taylor Coleridge and John Keats. William Morris’s poem “Two Red Roses Across the Moon,” seen depicted in a mural at the American Arts and Crafts Museum, shaped the knight-and-maiden narrative of “Will Thy Heart Be True?”, while Keats’s “La Belle Dame sans Merci” fed into “Summerland.”

From synthpop to ethereal wave

“Elysia” follows 2025’s synthpop-rooted “Submission” and that year’s “Fallen” EP, both released under Faded Pulse. Johnson traces the move toward a more ethereal sound to watching Monica Richards perform with Strange Boutique at the Black Cat in Washington, D.C. in 2025. “The moment I knew I wanted to move sonically towards that was when I saw Strange Boutique live,” Johnson said. “Seeing Monica Richards on stage and hearing the music live was really a light-bulb moment for me.”

Johnson names Projekt Records artists Black Tape for a Blue Girl, Lycia, Love Spirals Downwards and Unto Ashes as the strongest influences on the album, alongside the 1960s and ’70s folk of Pentangle and Donovan. The bassline on “Undine” was modeled on Slowdive’s “Ballad of Sister Sue,” and the hammered dulcimer that leads the instrumental “Fair Lady in Gold” came out of weeks spent studying Renaissance and medieval music. “Lamia’s Kiss” draws on Middle Eastern and Mediterranean sounds that Johnson traces partly to time spent living in Asia as a child, with the dulcimer again carrying the melody.

Johnson describes “Elysia” as more than escapism. “When listeners ‘leave the realm of Elysia,’ I want people to bring that sort of magic into their everyday lives,” Johnson said. “Whether that be getting involved in their local communities, making art, or reading poetry. Whatever it is that makes you feel connected to the world around you.”

About Faded Pulse

Faded Pulse is the solo project of Faeryn Johnson, based in Washington, D.C. Johnson entered the goth scene as a teenager, citing The Cure’s “Pornography” as a formative record for its dense sound design and Robert Smith’s lyricism. Faded Pulse’s first album, “Submission,” began in 2022 and was released in 2025, built primarily around 1980s new wave and synthpop influences. The “Fallen” EP followed later that year, moving toward a more ethereal sound.

“Elysia,” released in 2026, extends that shift further into ethereal wave, folk and goth, drawing on Johnson’s study of art history and Johnson’s long-standing interest in the 1990s Projekt Records catalogue. Johnson has described the album’s visual presentation, thrifted velvet, medieval-style dress and imagery drawn from John William Waterhouse’s paintings, as inseparable from its sound. “Elysia” is out now on Bandcamp.

items.title: Dark the Keeper and Ghost Reflection release ‘In the Arms of the Abyss’
items.summary: Dark the Keeper and Ghost Reflection released the split album "In the Arms of the Abyss" on Aliens Production, out November 12, 2026 on CD and digital.
items.fullText:
Dark the Keeper and Ghost Reflection, the two dark ambient and industrial projects of Slovak producer Alexander Borsov, released the split album ‘In the Arms of the Abyss’ on Aliens Production on November 12, 2026. The 16-track release is out on CD and digital.

The album splits its tracklist between Borsov’s two projects and three guest collaborations. Dark the Keeper contributes “Soul Burn,” “Dark Idea Generator,” “Soul Hunter,” “Trap Manipulation,” “Hidden Hatred,” “Labyrinth of Hell” and both bonus tracks, “Break in the Soul (Bonus Track)” and “Ghost (Bonus Track).” Ghost Reflection contributes “Integration of Madness,” “The Root of Evil,” “Games of Psychopaths,” “Infected” and “The Shattered World of Illusions.” The remaining three tracks are collaborations: “Break in the Soul (meets TC75)” with TC75, “Break in the Soul (Deconstruction by Deflect)” with Deflect, and “Ghost (meets dISHARMONY)” with dISHARMONY.

Ryby designed the release, and Anatoly “Tokee” Grinberg handled mastering.

“In the Arms of the Abyss” is available on CD and as a digital album on Bandcamp.

About Dark the Keeper and Ghost Reflection

Dark the Keeper and Ghost Reflection are two of several recording names used by Slovak producer Alexander Borsov, alongside Darkmechanic and Stellar Dynamics. Borsov is also a member of the group Diverje and got his start in metal bands including Morgue, Atom, Cremation Deads, Sarcoma and Satura before moving into electronic production. Both projects release through Aliens Production, a Slovak dark electronics label active since 1997 whose roster includes dISHARMONY, Oxyd, Headdreamer, Fractal and Human Vault.

As Dark the Keeper, Borsov released the album “Psychic Microbe” digitally in August 2026. As Ghost Reflection, he released the album “Dark Thinker” in June 2022 and the single “Dark Noise” in February 2024, before releasing the concept album “Dark Triad” on Aliens Production in September 2026. Borsov also released “Hypercontrol” as Darkmechanic on Aliens Production in October 2026. “In the Arms of the Abyss” brings Dark the Keeper and Ghost Reflection together on a single release for the first time, alongside guest contributions from TC75, Deflect and dISHARMONY.

items.title: Tom Shear remixes Unhappily Ever Now’s ‘To The Light’
items.summary: Tom Shear of Assemblage 23 remixed Unhappily Ever Now's "To The Light" into an EBM/synthpop/darkwave version, released November 11, 2026.
items.fullText:
Tom Shear of Assemblage 23 remixed Unhappily Ever Now’s single ‘”To The Light”‘, released on all major streaming platforms and Bandcamp on November 11, 2026. Shear’s version turns the original tribute into a darker EBM, synthpop and darkwave arrangement.

The original “To The Light,” written and performed by Stephen Watson, is a tribute to an aging cat, carrying themes of grief, love and remembrance. Shear created and mixed the remix; James Scott mastered it at Joy Thieves Productions. Unhappily Ever Now is Stephen Watson (primary songwriter, vocals, lyrics and melodies) and Maria V (vocals, lyrics and melodies). The band’s sound draws on the SYFY Channel series “12 Monkeys,” exploring disconnection and grief without closure in a time-bending setting.

“To The Light (Assemblage 23 Remix)” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and on all major streaming platforms.

About Unhappily Ever Now

Unhappily Ever Now is the project of Stephen Watson, also known for his work with Cleopatra Records act Green Jelly, alongside vocalist and lyricist Maria V. The band released the original “To The Light” in October 2025, with drums by Dan Milligan of The Joy Thieves, and mixing and mastering by Milligan and James Scott at Joy Thieves Productions. Tom Shear’s remix, arriving a year later, recasts the song in the EBM and darkwave register of his own Assemblage 23 productions.

items.title: Ghost Painted Sky release second album ‘Failure Blooms’
items.summary: Massachusetts darkwave band Ghost Painted Sky released their second album "Failure Blooms" on November 11, 2026, on CD and digital formats.
items.fullText:
Massachusetts darkwave and post-punk band Ghost Painted Sky released their second full-length album, ‘Failure Blooms’, on November 11, 2026. The eight-song record is out on CD and digital formats.

William Faith mixed and mastered “Failure Blooms” at his own Studio 13. The tracklist runs “There Against the Wall,” “Corridors,” “Kissing Lions,” “Sound and Fury,” “Ordinary Song,” “Dissolving Days,” “Insomnia” and “The Fire, The Flame.” The album includes the recent single “Kissing Lions” alongside a new recording of the band’s 2024 single “Insomnia.”

Lisa Wood sings and wrote the lyrics; David Strong plays guitar, bass, drums, ebow and synths, and also wrote lyrics; Michael Boudreau plays guitar throughout. Michael Rebeiro adds guitar on “Corridors” and “The Fire, The Flame,” and Aurora Grabill plays violin on “Corridors” and “Kissing Lions.” Wood made the cover artwork.

The album is accompanied by a video for “Sound and Fury.”

“Failure Blooms” is available on CD and as a digital album on Bandcamp.

About Ghost Painted Sky

Ghost Painted Sky began in 2014 as the solo studio project of David Strong, who released a self-titled debut EP that year, followed by the “The Shadow’s Breath” EP in 2015 and the band’s first live shows. Lisa Wood joined on vocals in 2018, starting with the “Scars” EP and continuing through the band’s debut full-length album, “Flightless.” The band appeared on the compilations “The Unquiet Grave 2020” (Cleopatra Records), “33 Gothic Bands You Should Know, Volume 8” (Post-Gothic, 2021), “You Are Still Not Alone” (Darkness Calling, 2021) and “Goths For Sanctuaries – The Album!!!” (2023), and released the “Ephemeral Wake” EP in 2021 and the singles “Corridors” (2022) and “Insomnia” (2024).

Work on “Failure Blooms” brought in new studio contributions from guitarist Michael Boudreau and longtime live keyboardist and violinist Aurora Grabill. The album’s first single, “Sound and Fury,” came out in late March 2026, followed in October by second single “Kissing Lions”. “Failure Blooms” now completes that rollout as the band’s second full-length album.

items.title: The Fair Attempts release ‘Doomscroller’ single and video
items.summary: Finnish industrial rock band The Fair Attempts released the single and video "Doomscroller" on November 11, 2026 via Starwing Digital.
items.fullText:
Finnish industrial rock band The Fair Attempts released the single and official music video ‘Doomscroller’ on November 11, 2026, via Starwing Digital.

“Doomscroller” addresses social media use and its hold on attention. said Timo Haakana, the band’s vocalist and frontman: “We’re losing ourselves to these machines. Who controls your eyes controls your mind. We are being manipulated daily through these devices that have essentially become extensions of our cognition. I wanted to make a rather lighthearted song and dance about it, while reminding us of what’s happening.”

Haakana wrote the lyrics; Stefan Brown mastered the track at Abbey Road Studios. The Fair Attempts comprises Timo Haakana (vocals, instruments) and Starwing (co-production, female vocals).

“Doomscroller” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp. The Fair Attempts are currently finishing their upcoming album, “These Walls,” due for release in spring 2027.

About The Fair Attempts

The Fair Attempts are a Finnish industrial rock act formed by Timo Haakana and Starwing, combining industrial rock and EBM with themes of technology, control and alienation. The band released the EP “Beyond the Edge of Nowhere” in 2023 and the single “Apart” in February 2025, before streaming their album “Null Guide” exclusively on Side-Line ahead of its official release in February 2026. “Doomscroller” is the band’s first single since “Null Guide,” arriving as the group works toward “These Walls,” due in spring 2027.

items.title: Rogue FX releases ‘Corporate World’ album on FiloFX Records
items.summary: Synth pop artist Rogue FX released his album "Corporate World" on November 6, 2026 via FiloFX Records, out on digital, CD, cassette and vinyl.
items.fullText:
Rogue FX, the synth pop project of Northern England producer Andrew Wood, released his new album ‘Corporate World’ on November 6, 2026, through FiloFX Records. The ten-track record is out on digital, CD, cassette and vinyl.

“Corporate World” draws on classic synth pop and 1980s electronic production. Wood built the album around themes of love, life, loss, success and power, examining the human cost of a world driven by profit and ambition.

The tracklist runs “The City Never Sleeps,” “Computer Love” (credited to Rogue FX and U.F.O 1982), “Root Of All Evil,” “The Place That I’m Going To,” “Working Week” (featuring Hollywood Brown), “Corporate World,” “Cost Of Loving,” “D.T.T.S.” (featuring Hollywood Brown), “Crash” and a closing remix, “Filofax (Greed Is Good Remix).”

Wood wrote and produced the album himself, handling all lyrics, music and production except on “Computer Love,” co-written with Jeanette Monja. Hollywood Brown plays guitar on “Working Week” and “D.T.T.S.,” Oswaldo Gonzalez plays guitar on “Computer Love,” and Wood plays guitar on “Root Of All Evil” and “Cost Of Loving.” Jason Hornig mastered the album at Electric Desk Mastering.

“Corporate World” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp, with CD, cassette and vinyl editions also available, and is streaming on Spotify.

About Rogue FX

Rogue FX is the recording name of Andrew Wood, an independent synth pop artist and producer based in Northern England. Alongside Rogue FX, Wood produces music as Liquid 1nc and presents a radio show on Radio Wigwam. “Corporate World” is released through his own label, FiloFX Records, and follows the project’s run of 1980s-influenced synth pop releases. The album’s examination of ambition and power through a synth pop lens marks Rogue FX’s latest full-length release under the FiloFX banner.

items.title: Beyond Obsession – In My Blood (Digital/CD Album – Scanner / Dark Dimensions)
items.summary: The German duo Beyond Obsession has been active for several years and has already released...
items.fullText:
The German duo Beyond Obsession has been active for several years and has already released a number of albums. For their latest release, which features 10 tracks, they collaborated with Scanner. The album explores themes such as obsession, loss, longing, and the things from which there is no escape.

First and foremost, Beyond Obsession remains a band operating within the broad spectrum of Electro-Pop. The compositions are pleasant, at times even ethereal, and occasionally reinforced by a harder edge. The choruses are generally catchy, and most of the songs are danceable. The music clearly draws on 1980s influences; at times, you almost get the feeling that Erasure might be just around the corner. The album is varied and contains several highly successful tracks. Unfortunately, I find the final section, comprising the last three songs, somewhat less inspired.

Beyond Obsession may not be breaking entirely new ground, but they certainly deserve their place within the Electro-Pop scene. All in all, this is an enjoyable album. (Rating:7).

Listen to “Into The Deep”:

About Beyond Obsession

Beyond Obsession is a German electro-pop duo of Nils Upahl and André Wylar. The project self-released “On My Way” (2012), “Tokio Underground” (2013) and “Listen, Learn And Speak” (2013) before the “Listen – The Remixes” set of 2014. Beyond Obsession signed to Popgefahr Records for “Black White Hearts” (2015), followed by “Pieces Of Machinery” (2015), “Moments Of Truth” (2016) and “Pure & Naked” (2017). The duo moved to Infacted Recordings for “Revolution From Below” (2020) and its “Speaking Of A Devil” remix EP the same year. “In My Blood” is released on the Scanner imprint of the German label Dark Dimensions.

items.title: Darkwave Duo Twin Tribes Cast Their Spell Over San Antonio — Review and Photo Gallery
items.summary: From Brownsville, Texas, to an international circuit of clubs, theatres, and festivals, Twin Tribes have become one of contemporary darkwave’s defining success stories. Formed in 2017 by Luis Navarro and… The post Darkwave Duo Twin Tribes Cast Their Spell Over
items.fullText:
From Brownsville, Texas, to an international circuit of clubs, theatres, and festivals, Twin Tribes have become one of contemporary darkwave’s defining success stories. Formed in 2017 by Luis Navarro and Joel Niño, Jr., the duo brought together an affection for post-punk, coldwave, and the electronic music of the 1980s, giving their songs a distinctive balance of melodic immediacy and occult intrigue. Navarro’s low, romantic vocals and bright guitar figures meet Niño’s commanding basslines, with synthesizers and drum machines supplying the architecture. Their music invites you onto the dance floor, then gives you a chorus to carry home.

Their debut album, Shadows, arrived in 2018, establishing the darkwave vocabulary they would develop across Ceremony in 2019 and Pendulum in 2024. Songs such as Shadows, Heart & Feather, Fantasmas, and Monolith explain the appeal: memorable bass and guitar lines, a sure instinct for a hook, and an emotional directness that gives the gothic imagery its human scale. The 2021 remix collection Altars, featuring contributions from She Past Away, Ash Code, Wingtips, and others, also placed their songs in conversation with the wider international scene.

Years of touring across North America, Europe, and Latin America have helped turn those records into a shared language. Twin Tribes’ rise rests on the connection between the songs and the people singing them back, sustained through an independent approach the pair have discussed on Ari’s Take. They have become one of the biggest bands on the international darkwave circuit, with the reach to bring that music before audiences well beyond its usual rooms. Their newly announced place at Coachella 2027 adds another clear marker to that ascent. In San Antonio on November 6, however, the immediate challenge was winning over a room assembled for a considerably heavier evening.

San Antonio-based photographer Chris Stokes was there to document the performance and report from the crowd. His concert and portrait work includes fellow travelers such as Riki, Mareux, and Past Self, as well as Twin Tribes themselves. Below, Stokes recounts the duo’s appearance alongside Acid Bath, Kylesa, and The Atlas Moth at the Boeing Center at Tech Port, followed by his photo gallery from the evening.

Live review and photography by Chris Stokes

On a bill built for sludge, feedback and low-end ruin, Twin Tribes were the strangest guests of the night, and that was the point. The Boeing Center at Tech Port is a big, blunt room, and the evening belonged to heavy music, Louisiana metal legends Acid Bath headlined, with Kylesa and The Atlas Moth rounding out a lineup of swampy, psychedelic, bone-heavy riffs. Into that came a band whose weapons are chorus-washed guitars, a pulsing bassline and a synth that glows like a neon sign in a rainstorm. Opening with “Path to Antares” and sliding into “Another Life,” Twin Tribes made no concession to the other acts around them. They simply played their own songs at full volume.

The sound is what made the mismatch work. In a hall tuned for crushing weight, Twin Tribes offered the opposite, melody with a razor edge, cold and cinematic. “Portal to the Void” and “Heart & Feather” kept the momentum driving, and the bass filled the space with a deep rumble that held its own among the metal faithful. By “Sangre de Oro” and “Upir” the set had found its own gravity. The Spanish titles and the gothic romanticism felt right in San Antonio, a city that has always had a place for dark, beautiful music. Deep into the set, “Cauldron of Thorns” and “Shadows” leaned fully into the band’s synth-driven side, all shimmer and yearning, a world away from the thunder shaking the rest of the bill.

By the time the band reached “Lobo Hombre En Paris” and “Monolith,” the contrast had stopped feeling like a clash. Heads that had been nodding along to the beat were swaying to the synths, and the crowd was settling into another world. Closing with “Fantasmas,” Twin Tribes left the stage the way the best post-punk acts always have, having changed the temperature of a room that wasn’t built for them. Metal and goth have shared a bloodline for decades, and for one night in San Antonio, alongside Acid Bath, Kylesa and The Atlas Moth, the family resemblance was hard to miss

Twin Tribes in San Antonio — photo gallery by Chris Stokes

Explore Chris Stokes’s photographs from Twin Tribes’ November 6 performance below. All photographs by Chris Stokes. Find more of his concert and portrait work at c-stokes.com.

Twin Tribes — Recent Releases and Upcoming Appearances:

The San Antonio appearance follows a busy stretch for the duo, including Red Rocks Amphitheatre in Morrison, Colorado, on September 15, 2026, on a bill with Acid Bath and Ministry, and Sick New World in Fort Worth, Texas, on October 24. On record, Live at Fascination Street received an expanded release in 2026, reaching worldwide streaming services on August 28 alongside vinyl and CD editions. Recorded in Nashville in December 2019 and first issued in May 2020, the performance returns to material from the band’s first two albums. Listen and order here.

Other recent releases include the 2025 singles Ecos and Play Alone, as well as Monolith Remixes: V and their Audiotree Live session. items.title: Brooklyn’s PONS Puts Ego and Excess into Overdrive on “RACECAR” — Watch Video for “Million Dollar Man”
items.summary: The trouble with becoming a million-dollar man is that somebody has to keep agreeing on the valuation. Every admiring glance becomes confirmation, every slight a threat to the entire enterprise.… The post Brooklyn’s PONS Puts Ego and Excess into Overdrive on “
items.fullText:
The trouble with becoming a million-dollar man is that somebody has to keep agreeing on the valuation. Every admiring glance becomes confirmation, every slight a threat to the entire enterprise. In the video for MILLION DOLLAR MAN, Brooklyn’s PONS turn that dependence on approval into a garish spectacle, with Jack Parker grinning through sunglasses as his image splits, smears, and changes colour. It is an apt introduction to RACECAR, their new album, released November 5 through Casa Gogol Records, the label founded by Gogol Bordello’s Eugene Hütz.

Parker traces the song’s beginnings to a month in Morocco following the collapse of an earlier PONS lineup and a cancelled European tour. In Marrakech, the repetition and call-and-response of Amazigh trance music performed by street musicians suggested a connection with the dance records occupying his headphones. Listening to releases from Sahel Sounds and artists such as Koudede helped develop that interest into MILLION DOLLAR MAN. Returning to Morocco after PONS’ 2026 European tour, he filmed its video with frequent collaborator Gigi Barwald.

The result subjects Parker’s extravagant mugging to an almost continuous electronic makeover. Rooftops and blue-painted hillside buildings sit behind a figure who keeps dissolving into acidic colour, television static, and overlapping versions of himself. Oversized sunglasses and a bottle of wine supply the props; the editing supplies the identity crisis. Parker describes the intended mixture as “half part Naked Lunch and half part Hotline Miami.” The joke comes through clearly: a man desperate to occupy the entire picture can scarcely keep his own face intact.

Parker explains:

“Lyrically, ‘MILLION DOLLAR MAN’ explores over the top embodiments of hyper masculinity, narcissism, ego, fragility, and money. It’s from the point of view of someone who has become self aware of the power that they hold and how they can exploit it to benefit themselves as well as the deep insecurity that often influences brash and obnoxious behavior. The album Tranquility Base Hotel and Casino was a very big lyrical inspiration for me on this track specifically and throughout the album as a whole.”

Watch the video for MILLION DOLLAR MAN below:

RACECAR took shape across 28 consecutive days in New York City during the summer of 2025, after an offer to support Gogol Bordello left Parker a month to assemble music and a band. That pressure carries into arrangements which keep finding another gear, another voice, another instrument demanding admission. Electroclash, dance-punk, industrial electronics, and orchestral flourishes crowd together with considerable purpose: these songs concern people whose appetite for attention, wealth, and advancement has outgrown their ability to enjoy any of it. The futuristic setting draws on Blade Runner and Brave New World, while the lyrics keep reaching back toward Rome. Progress has acquired some very old ambitions.

AUTOGRAPH opens the album with hollow metallic percussion, its tropical bounce suggesting a rhythm section assembled from pipes and whatever else might ring when struck. Parker’s phrasing carries a touch of Damon Albarn’s conversational mischief before a bright, feminine vocal sends the song towards hyperpop. Shouted responses, buoyant beats, and overlapping voices pull 1990s electronica into contact with British alternative pop, then a solo builds towards an electroclash finish. The changes arrive with the cheerful unpredictability of someone repeatedly grabbing the wheel.

Its celebrity aspirant has a similarly flexible personality, replacing yesterday’s self whenever a more profitable version becomes available. Contacts, access, money, and desirability blur into one sales pitch. Beneath the demand for an autograph sits a more ordinary wish to be wanted, and the eventual appeal to a lover lets a little tenderness slip through the self-promotion. The opener establishes a useful tension for the whole record: these grotesques remain susceptible to recognisable human needs.

Watch the video for AUTOGRAPH below:

CITY SLICKER takes its time furnishing the nightclub. A rippling synthesizer sequence places Kraftwerk’s precision beside the glide of 1970s electronic disco; sizzling percussion, descending keyboard chords, brassy tones, and bending pitches gradually fill the space. When the male and female voices finally shout together, the track has become a wonderfully elastic dance-floor proposition. Its lyrics introduce the city as a system of fees and favours, where pleasure repeats on command and status always costs more than expected. The invitation to bite the hand that never feeds neatly overturns the usual advice about gratitude: what, exactly, has the arrangement provided? Echoing, manipulated vocals, a distorted kick, and jungle-like sounds make the break increasingly disorienting before acoustic guitar strumming supplies a beautifully incongruous exit.

Watch the video for CITY SLICKER below:

BRONSON brings the city’s suspicious activity into sharper focus. A muffled snare clears, an electronic melody charges forward, and Parker starts recounting sightings with the irritated vigilance of a commuter whose journey has become somebody else’s criminal operation. Banks, briefcases, hourly news checks, and apparently interchangeable faces accumulate around the practical business of paying bills and keeping a client fed. The repeated declarations of what he saw offer certainty, although the details suggest a man struggling to interpret the transaction unfolding in front of him. Metallic flutter and additional layers tighten the arrangement as his dry post-punk delivery grows more openly agitated. By the final third, the account has become frantic; the departing pitch-shifted synths leave its questions unanswered. The song catches how easily economic necessity can make complicity sound like common sense.

MILLION DOLLAR MAN, the fourth track, turns that anxiety into a public performance of invincibility. Deep, rippling synths initially suggest darkwave before a higher electronic figure, shuffling drums, and metallic clatter pull the song towards electroclash. Parker half-speaks and half-sings his pitch, punctuated by a reverberating feminine “yeah,” until the dance beat takes hold with a Sextile-like bounce. His voice then approaches a Trent Reznor-style scream as the arrangement hardens into body music, with shouted exchanges and peculiar harmonies crowding the rhythm.

The lyrics expose the dependence beneath the display: a man who claims exceptional power still needs somebody to tell him he is the only one. Click farming, backroom influence, and inherited privilege sit beside the almost childlike wish to occupy another person’s first waking thought. Just as the groove becomes comfortable, a buzzing synth break and muttered delivery interrupt the performance. The ensuing drum barrage sounds like an attempt to overwhelm a doubt that has already been heard.

ON THE LAM sends the whole enterprise hurtling through a malfunctioning amusement park. A bright, unstable synth melody, hyperactive beat, and repeated yowl give the track the giddy movement of an old platform game played far too quickly. Parker’s more unhinged phrases suggest Nick Cave during the Birthday Party years, while the harmonies tug the performance towards synth-punk. There is something wonderfully cartoonish about the contrast between that spring-loaded music and lyrics full of concealed tracks, suspected informers, and revised reputations. Straightening a tie becomes almost indistinguishable from tightening a noose. By the time Parker starts singing about rewriting his image for posterity, the flight has become a publicity campaign, with a pistol and a list of names lending urgency to the rebrand.

HOT AIR [PRELUDE] briefly gives the record a different scale. Repeating, horn-like figures and fluttering flute sounds introduce an orchestral flourish before passing directly into the song proper. Its compact fanfare prepares the entrance of another person with a great deal to say.

HOT AIR follows with brassy momentum, emphatic piano strikes, and punk vocals riding a buoyant new wave rhythm. The arrangement’s big-band extravagance recalls JG Thirlwell and Foetus, with a little of Diamond Dogs’ theatrical scale in the way it makes a personal grievance seem fit for a public spectacle. Parker begins by dismissing somebody’s talk, yet the complaint soon reveals the hurt beneath it: declarations of love have failed to prevent abandonment, and promises of change have become another form of exhausted conversation. A gentler passage of violin and smooth crooning opens that wound before the full arrangement returns. The late insistence that things are improving sounds increasingly precarious against an unwelcoming city and the suspicion that the worst may still be approaching.

IF NOT NOW…, which Post-Punk.com has previously featured, makes impatience both its subject and its organising principle. A tapping, Morse-like electronic figure meets rubbery synth stabs before the drums propel the opening forward. The vocal attack catches something of the Knack’s My Sharona, then expands into the heightened delivery of the post-punk revival. Male and female voices arrive in rapid exchanges as the song switches between its loping stride and a more accelerated rush. Processed grunts and clanging piano complicate the movement; violins enter around the midpoint, making the arrangement feel increasingly extravagant.

The demand to act now grows more troubling as references to Romulus, conquest, privileged dealings, and divine favour gather around it. Desire becomes an excuse for possession as Parker sings of claiming a place among those who decide how history will be remembered. A slower passage of languid vocals, chiming piano, and reedy tones eventually gives way to a drinking-song stomp and saxophone, allowing that hunger for power to become alarmingly convivial. Animator Arturo Baston’s accompanying video supplies an appropriately grotesque carnival ride.

Watch the video for IF NOT NOW… below:

PLIGHT OF THE FOOL makes the machinery harder to escape. A thick, propulsive drumbeat presses against wiry synth textures while the vocal races through obedience, disposable people, focus groups, and company policy. The language reduces human beings to data and marketable characteristics, then asks what a head is for if thinking brings no useful reward. A dull, jackhammer-like repetition enters the increasingly dense mix, and Parker’s delivery acquires an industrial abrasion somewhere between Nine Inch Nails and Filter. The subsequent slowdown is particularly effective: the voice drops into a distorted lower register, and the beat assumes a heavy, almost processional weight. All that earlier scrambling has led to an arrangement which feels brutally difficult to move.

MASK EATS FACE inherits that oppressive weight and develops it into the album’s major finale. A thick kick, industrial buzzing, and cold electronic chimes accumulate tension beneath the lowered, distorted voice. As the rhythm accelerates and the vocal becomes clearer, an organ-like synth figure bends upwards into a squeal. There is more of Foetus’ grotesque theatricality in the collision of synth-punk urgency and oversized menace, although the track keeps finding its own strange routes through the pressure. A vocal break gives space to a mournful, coded electronic figure and buzzing sounds moving across the stereo field; colder synths then gather around the rapid percussion before a bass-driven passage leads into a denouement with an expansive, progressive-synth character.

Here, the album’s obsession with advancement reaches its most direct reckoning. Parker sings of finally obtaining what he wanted, only to discover that the public identity has consumed the person underneath. Deals, war, masculine self-assertion, and fantasies of a glorious legacy collapse into the same ruinous appetite. The image of wax wings gives the ambition an unmistakable destination, even as the closing words reach towards escape. PONS allow that possibility to remain unsettled; wanting freedom is hardly proof that this particular man knows how to stop.

CRASHTEST follows as a minute-long postscript, with strings, woodwinds, saxophone, and trombone. Its title completes the record’s running argument about acceleration. After so many characters mistake forward movement for progress, the prospect of impact makes a fitting final thought.

RACECAR is a terrific exercise in excess with a sharp ear for its costs. PONS make ambition danceable, vanity ridiculous, and the pursuit of pleasure increasingly difficult to separate from panic. The hooks give those ideas immediate appeal, while the sudden changes of voice, pace, and instrumentation keep exposing the instability underneath. For all its crowded arrangements, the album has a remarkably clear sense of the people trapped inside them: forever upgrading the image, forever hungry for the next affirmation, and increasingly unsure who is supposed to be enjoying the ride.

Listen to RACECAR below, order the album here, or find additional streaming options here.

Built around Parker’s songwriting and a determined DIY touring ethic, PONS have shared stages with Gogol Bordello, Bush Tetras, A Place To Bury Strangers, Lambrini Girls, Laura Jane Grace, and Geese. RACECAR brings that live appetite into an unusually broad ensemble: Ozzie Silva contributes drums, Steve La Rosa provides string arrangements and production, and Zoltán Sindhu handles production, engineering, and mixing, with mastering by Dave Cooley. Contributions from string players, woodwinds, brass, marimba, and backing vocalists help Parker push the songs into their many improbable shapes.
